title: Hackers Steal 1.8 Million Records From Nikkei
description: Nikkei, a major Japanese media company, disclosed a data breach affecting over 1.8 million records. The breach involved unauthorized access to a cloud service using previously compromised credentials. Approximately 150,000 records contained personally identifiable information such as names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth. No credit card or financial information was compromised. Nikkei revoked the compromised credentials promptly and notified regulators. As of the latest update, there is no evidence of misuse of the stolen data or disruption to services.
aiSummary: On October 7, 2026, attackers used previously compromised credentials to access a cloud service used by Nikkei for system development, resulting in the theft of approximately 1.83 million records. Of these, about 1.68 million records contained non-identifiable information, 150,000 records contained personally identifiable information (names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, dates of birth), and 120,000 records contained email addresses only. No financial data such as credit card information was accessed. Nikkei responded by revoking the compromised credentials immediately, notifying regulators, and continuing an investigation. No evidence of data misuse or operational disruption has been found.
aiImpact: The breach exposed personal information of approximately 150,000 individuals, including sensitive identifiers such as names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth. This could potentially increase the risk of identity theft or phishing attacks for those affected. However, no financial data was compromised, and no misuse of the stolen data has been detected to date. The incident did not cause service disruptions or data tampering.
